purpose: FTMO 2-Step at the 9% dial — WIDEN the book from 4 to 8 sleeves to kill daily-limit breaches. FTMO's binding constraint is the 5% DAILY loss, not the 10% overall, and at a 9% dial the deployed 4-sleeve book's worst scaled day is -5.07% (x1.5 floating proxy) which BREACHES. Widening thins that tail back inside the limit. Measured pass over 5 seeds: core 4 = 88.6% with fail_day 9.3%; wide 8 = 91.2% / 4.0%; wide 8 + reversal = 94.1% / 0.0%.
_vol_note: Only worth deploying AT the 9% dial. At 7% the 4-sleeve book already has zero daily breaches and widening merely dilutes return (measured: FundingPips Flex @7% pass 99.7% core vs 99.1% wide). Match the book to the BINDING constraint: daily-limit-binding -> widen; max-loss-binding -> maximise Sharpe with a narrower book (see configs/v5_maven_book.json).
_classes_note: 8 sleeves across 7 classes, equal-class-risk. Book Sharpe +1.357 (vs core 4's +1.428) — deliberately ACCEPTING slightly lower Sharpe to buy a thinner left tail, because at a 9% dial the daily limit is what fails the challenge, not the return. maxDD improves -7.7% -> -6.8%.
_honesty_note: This does NOT improve returns. Matched-vol paired t vs the deployed 4-sleeve book is -0.61 (3 of 8 years better), and the 2022-26 half is WORSE (Sharpe 1.04 vs 1.20). The entire justification is daily-breach elimination at the 9% dial. If FTMO is ever run at 7% instead, use configs/v5_ftmo_challenge.json.
